content:
Apple is continuing to improve the profile features on Apple TV 4K, with a change in tvOS 27 related to app access permissions, giving users more reason to use profiles.

tvOS 27 lets you restrict users from opening specific apps

Profiles are a common feature on major streaming platforms and, among other benefits, ensure that housemates' individual watch histories and recommendations remain separate.

Apple added profiles to tvOS long ago, but after a number of upgrades over the past year, the feature has become more useful.

Now tvOS 27 brings another improvement. According to Apple's official release notes:

This change is clearly aimed at parents.

A child's profile already lets you restrict the types of content they can see in the Apple TV app. Although this is a useful feature, it does not stop your child from opening another app that does not have such restrictions.

Now, however, parents can go into Settings and completely block the launch of selected apps when a child's profile is active.

This is a welcome step toward making the profile feature more complete, and it is in line with Apple's recent focus on upgrading parental controls in iOS 27.

Speaking of profile improvements, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 will bring Apple's profile system to the iPhone and iPad for the first time. You can learn more here.

Are you using profiles on your Apple TV? What new features would you like to see? Let us know in the comments.
